hairTypes.title: Type 1 Straight
hairTypes.description: Straight textures range from very fine and silky to slightly coarse with visible body.
hairTypes.pattern: Usually reflects light easily and can get weighed down by heavy products.

hairTypes.title: Type 2 Wavy
hairTypes.description: Wavy hair forms loose S patterns and often needs balance between definition and softness.
hairTypes.pattern: Can lose shape with very rich formulas or become frizzy with not enough hydration.

hairTypes.title: Type 3 Curly
hairTypes.description: Curly hair forms springy loops that usually benefit from slip, moisture, and styling support.
hairTypes.pattern: Definition improves when products layer well and drying routines reduce disruption.

hairTypes.title: Type 4 Coily
hairTypes.description: Coily textures often have tight bends and can benefit from moisture retention and thoughtful layering.
hairTypes.pattern: Shrinkage is common and richer conditioning routines often help with manageability.

porosity.description: Hair has trouble letting moisture in, so lighter products and warmth can help products absorb more evenly.
porosity.guidance: Choose lightweight layers and avoid stacking heavy butters too early.

porosity.description: Hair usually absorbs and retains moisture in a balanced way.
porosity.guidance: Most product families can work, so focus on goal and density fit.

porosity.description: Hair often absorbs moisture quickly and loses it quickly, so richer support can help seal it in.
porosity.guidance: Look for richer conditioners, creams, and sealing oils when they fit your density.

density.description: Scalp is easier to see and heavy formulas can flatten the hair quickly.
density.guidance: Favor airy textures and strategic styling support.

density.description: Hair fullness feels balanced, so many product textures can work.
density.guidance: Adjust mostly for porosity and styling goals.

density.description: Hair appears fuller and may need richer formulas or stronger hold to reach all sections evenly.
density.guidance: Sectioning and richer products often improve consistency.
